beat_player.text: {player} won the field with {troop_count} men. I lost ground today and I will learn from it, as I did in the first war.
Well fought, {player}. You took {gold} in spoils, and my men will remember the lesson. Come find me at the Imzaz ford.
You have the better of me this day, {player}. Do not mistake one field for the whole war. Spring water is patient and so am I.
Do not look so pleased, {player}. You earned those {gold} coins fairly, and I would rather lose to you than to a cheat.

beat_by_player.text: I lost {troop_count} men to {player} at the salt pans today. Good ground was taken by a good hand, and I bear no grudge.
A fair field, {player}. I have given up {troop_count} men and some pride, but the pride will mend faster than the men.
Well struck, {player}. I did not expect you to press so hard from the eastern dunes. Shake my hand before you ride off, and the water is on me.
{player} has beaten me again. Mark my words, I will be back on that ground with more patience and sharper spears.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} and I held the line against {enemy_faction} today with {troop_count} men between us. That is how the old wars were won.
You fought like a veteran out there, {player}. The ground we took together is ground we both keep now.
We hold the same side for once, {player}. Keep your shield up and your eyes on {enemy_faction}, and we will talk of this at the ford.
Good work with {troop_count} men at the ridge. {enemy_faction} will remember that they met two stubborn banners today.

released_by_player.text: You could have named a ransom, {player}, yet you opened the gate instead. I will not forget that mercy.
{player} let me walk free from the cells today. Few would have done so, and fewer still without asking for a price.
Do not think this buys you my friendship, {player}. A released captive remembers the one who freed him, and I remember you.
Mercy in the field is rarer than good salt, {player}. I owe you a cup of mead at the ford when you next pass through.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Our banners have room for those who learn to stand their ground, and you look like you will.
I am glad you swore to {my_faction}, {player}. Come find me at the Imzaz ford in the evening and I will show you the old paths.
You have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. Judge the oath by what you do in the coming seasons, not by what you say today.
{player} now bears the colors of {my_faction}. I will watch how you carry them, and I expect nothing less than honest work.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} is in good hands, {player}. I have seen many lords fall from too much land, so guard it well and the people will guard you.
The lord granted you {fief}, {player}. I am not one to grumble over the ledger, but I held that ground longer than you did.
So {fief} went to you, {player}. I will hold my tongue for now, but I will watch the walls you build and the men you keep.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. The first winter in a new keep teaches more than any tutor, so start early and listen.

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}, good to see a friendly banner on this road. I am {persona} of {my_faction}. Water is short out here, so share it freely.
{player}, we meet on the open road. I am {persona} of {my_faction}. Keep your distance and we will have no quarrel today.
{player}. I know your banner, and I know your name. {persona} of {my_faction} does not forget a field where my men bled. Ride carefully.
Steady, {player}, I see your party on the road. It is {persona} here, of {my_faction}. Let us trade news before the sun dips.

encounter_farewell.text: Go safely, {player}. May your water hold and your horses stay sound until we meet at the ford again.
We have talked enough for one day, {player}. Ride on, and mind the dunes where the sand swallows careless riders.
Our road parts here, {player}. Do not let it cross mine again without a good reason, for I have not forgotten you.
Farewell, {player}. Take a cup of water with you from the ford, and remember that the long road is kinder to patient men.

ambient_chatter.text: The heat over {town} is thick today. I have crossed the salt pans in worse, but my lips still crack by midday.
Word from {village} says the wells are running low again. Desert folk know this country well, so bring spare skins.
The fog came down over the marsh near {village} this morning, and I trusted my boots over my eyes.
Those who ride to {town} should take the eastern road, where the dunes hide less thirst. I have walked it many times.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost nearly all of {troop_count} men in that valley. Such a day breaks some captains, so rest and regroup before you march again.
Do not let today's loss weigh on you, {player}. I lost a full company once in the first war and still I went back to the field.
A hard blow for {player} today, with {troop_count} men gone from the rolls. Count what remains, take the lessons, and carry on.
{player}, your banners are scattered after the valley, and {troop_count} of your men will not see another spring. Maybe now you will listen to someone older.
